newsitem.title: USA: Fieldcrest sued for patent infringement.
newsitem.headline: Fieldcrest sued for patent infringement.

text.p: A start-up home decorating manufacturer Monday filed a patent infringement suit against Fieldcrest Cannon Inc. alleging that the textile giant is wrongfully using the smaller company's information to make a grip for holding slipcovers.

In the lawsuit filed in Manhattan federal court, New York-based PRescient Partners L.P. accused Fieldcrest and its Sure Fit Inc. unit of patent infringement, misappropriation of trade secrets and false advertising.
Fieldcrest and Sure Fit are the nation's largest makers of casual slipcovers.
The suit seeks unspecified damages and the recall and destruction of the allegedly infringing grips.

Fieldcrest Cannon, based in Kannapolis, N.C., makes home furnishing products, mainly towels and sheeting, under the Fieldcrest, Cannon, Royal Velvet, Charisma, Touch of Class, St. Mary's, Cannon Royal Family, Caldwell, Sure Fit and private label brands.
Its stock fell 37.5 cents to $14.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
